descriptors.concept_name: Legal Nature and Position of Directors
descriptors.definition: Directors act as agents of the company to bind it in transactions and as trustees to safeguard its properties and funds. They stand in a fiduciary relationship with the company rather than with individual shareholders.
inclusion: Individuals appointed to the Board to manage business affairs
Directors elected from shareholders or outsiders
exclusion: Bodies corporate, firms, or associations of persons
Individual shareholders acting outside official capacity
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from shareholders who are owners, whereas directors manage business affairs and owe fiduciary duties to the company as a corporate entity.

descriptors.definition: Every company must constitute a Board of Directors consisting solely of individuals, adhering to specified minimum and maximum numerical thresholds. Public companies require a minimum of three directors, private companies two, and One Person Companies one, with an overall maximum cap of fifteen unless expanded via special resolution.
instrument_references: Companies (Appointment and Qualifications of Directors) Rules, 2014, Rule 3
inclusion: Minimum director requirements for public companies, private companies, and OPCs
Appointment of at least one woman director for prescribed classes of companies
exclusion: Non-individual entities such as bodies corporate, firms, or association of persons
Exceeding 15 directors without passing a special resolution
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general member composition by strictly mandating individual natural persons and setting specific structural minimums and maximums.

descriptors.definition: Directors are generally appointed by the company in a general meeting, except where specific statutory provisions allow alternative board-level appointments. Individual subscribers to the memorandum act as first directors if articles are silent, and every appointed director must possess an active Director Identification Number.
inclusion: Individual subscribers acting as first directors when articles are silent
Subsequent director appointments made by shareholders in general meetings
Mandatory allotment of Director Identification Number prior to appointment
exclusion: Corporate bodies acting as subscribers becoming first directors
Appointment of any person lacking a valid Director Identification Number
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes first directors determined by memorandum subscription from subsequent directors elected by shareholders in general meetings.

descriptors.definition: Director Identification Number is a unique identification number allotted by the Central Government to any individual intending to be appointed as a director or serving as an existing director. This mandatory identifier includes designated partnership identification numbers issued under separate limited liability partnership regulations.
instrument_references: Companies (Specification of Definitions Details) Rules, 2014, Rule 2(1)(e)
inclusion: Identification numbers allotted to individuals intending to be appointed as directors
Previously obtained DINs and recognized DPINs equivalent for designated partners
exclusion: Appointment of any person as a director without an allotted DIN
Separate DPIN acquisition requirements for individuals already possessing an eligible DIN
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general company registration numbers by being an individual-specific tracking identifier required for holding any directorship.

descriptors.definition: Persons other than retiring directors may stand for directorship if they or a proposing member submit a written notice at least fourteen days prior to a general meeting along with a mandatory monetary deposit. The company must inform its members of such candidature at least seven days before the meeting through electronic or written notices and website publication.
instrument_references: Companies (Appointment and Qualifications of Directors) Rules, 2014, Rule 13
inclusion: Candidature notices submitted by non-retiring candidates or proposing members
Required monetary deposit accompanying the notice
Exemptions from deposit requirements for independent directors or committee-recommended candidates
exclusion: Retiring directors seeking standard reappointment through regular rotation mechanisms
Candidates lacking the mandatory notice period or financial deposit where applicable
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard retiring director re-appointments by requiring explicit proactive written notice and financial deposits from non-retiring candidates or supporting members.

descriptors.definition: A listed company may have one director elected by small shareholders holding shares of a specified nominal value, provided a qualifying threshold of members submits a formal notice. This representative director is considered an independent director for governance purposes.
instrument_references: Companies (Appointment and Qualifications of Directors) Rules, 2014, Rule 7
inclusion: Election of a single director by small shareholders in listed companies
Notice requirements backed by specified numbers of small shareholders
Classification of the small shareholders' director as an independent director
exclusion: Unlisted companies lacking statutory thresholds for small shareholder directorships
Shareholders holding nominal values exceeding the prescribed small shareholder limit
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general board appointments by specifically empowering minority small shareholders through a dedicated collective petition mechanism.

descriptors.concept_name: Board Appointment of Additional and Alternate Directors
descriptors.definition: The Board of Directors may appoint additional directors if empowered by the articles, provided the appointee has not been rejected at a general meeting, with tenure expiring at the next annual general meeting. Alternate directors may also be appointed during a director's long absence, subject to statutory and governance limitations.
inclusion: Board appointment of additional directors via article authorization
Tenure limitations restricting additional directors to the date of the next annual general meeting
Alternate director appointments covering extended absences
exclusion: Appointing any person as an additional director who failed to secure appointment at a general meeting
Extending an additional director's term beyond the due date of the annual general meeting
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from regular shareholder-elected directors by originating from Board-level discretion authorized strictly through company articles to manage urgent management requirements.

descriptors.concept_name: Individual Voting Requirement for Director Appointments
descriptors.definition: Companies are prohibited from appointing two or more directors through a single collective resolution unless a preliminary proposal to do so is agreed upon without any dissenting votes. This ensures shareholders retain individual choice and can reject specific candidates without voting against an entire slate.
instrument_references: Companies (Appointment and Qualifications of Directors) Rules, 2014
inclusion: Separate resolutions required for each individual director appointment
Unanimous agreement exception allowing single resolution voting if no votes are cast against the proposal
exclusion: Passing a single resolution to elect multiple directors when any member casts a dissenting vote
Exemptions applicable to specific government companies, wholly-owned subsidiaries, and private companies under rules
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from block-voting practices by forcing strict individual assessment of candidates unless absolute unanimous consent permits a grouped ballot.

descriptors.definition: Companies may adopt systems of proportional representation in their articles to ensure minority shareholders secure fair representation on the board. This mechanism overrides standard majority voting rules by utilizing single transferable votes, cumulative voting, or other transparent methods for at least two-thirds of total directors.
inclusion: Adopting proportional representation via company articles for at least two-thirds of total directors
Methods including single transferable votes and cumulative voting systems
Triennial appointment cycles
exclusion: Default appointment of all directors via standard simple majority voting
Failing to provide minority interest representation mechanisms in articles when opting for the system
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard simple majority voting by allowing minority voting blocks to secure proportional board representation rather than being entirely overridden.

descriptors.definition: A person is ineligible for appointment as a director if they suffer from specified personal incapacities, legal convictions, un-paid call defaults, or non-compliance with identification and directorship limits. Additional disqualifications attach automatically if a director serves on a company defaulting on financial statements, annual returns, or deposit repayments.
inclusion: Personal legal incapacities such as unsound mind or insolvency
Criminal convictions carrying specified prison sentences
Defaults in paying share calls or filing statutory financial statements
exclusion: Mandatory professional or educational qualification requirements, which are not prescribed by law
Holding qualification shares as a pre-requisite
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from performance-based removals by functioning as absolute statutory bars preventing initial appointment or continuation based on past legal defaults or personal status.

descriptors.definition: An individual cannot hold office as a director, including alternate directorships, in more than twenty companies concurrently, with a sub-limit restricting public company directorships to a maximum of ten. Dormant companies and section 8 companies are excluded from these numerical counts.
inclusion: Overall cap of twenty companies for simultaneous directorships
Sub-limit capping public company directorships at ten
Exclusion of dormant and compliant section 8 companies from the computation
exclusion: Holding directorships exceeding ten public companies or twenty total companies
Counting compliant section 8 companies towards the maximum limit
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from single-company governance roles by setting a hard statutory ceiling across multiple corporate entities simultaneously.

descriptors.definition: Listed public companies must maintain at least one-third of their total directors as independent directors, while specific classes of unlisted public companies must appoint a minimum of two based on paid-up capital, turnover, or loan thresholds. Intermittent vacancies must be filled within specified statutory timeframes.
instrument_references: Companies (Appointment and Qualifications of Directors) Rules, 2014, Rule 4(1)
inclusion: One-third independent director quota for listed public companies
Minimum of two independent directors for unlisted public companies meeting financial thresholds
Mandatory filling of intermittent vacancies by the next board meeting or three months
exclusion: Private companies lacking public company listing or financial threshold triggers
Mandatory appointments when financial conditions fail to be met for three consecutive years
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from executive or non-executive ordinary directors by strict statutory independence criteria and quantitative financial scale triggers.
